1. Abstract

The pursuit of recursive self-improvement in large language models relies on the fundamental premise that an artificial agent can autonomously evaluate, refine, and integrate modifications to its own logic and architecture. However, this paradigm faces a severe theoretical limitation: when a system acts as both the generator of novel solutions and the sole evaluator of those solutions, the mathematical gap between its generative and evaluative capabilities inevitably collapses. Without an independent ground truth, the model optimizes for internal plausibility rather than external validity, leading to a phenomenon formalized as Recursive Epistemic Collapse. This report details a comprehensive architectural framework for preventing this collapse through Grounded Causal Verification. By anchoring the self-modification feedback loop in a dual-engine verification sandbox—combining the rigorous symbolic proofs of interactive theorem provers such as Lean 4 and Rocq with empirical execution simulators—the proposed framework forces the agent to satisfy invariant external checks.

This architecture is operationalized through a heavily structured implementation strategy. It begins with the construction of a dual-verification sandbox, followed by the deployment of a Causal Symbolic Reinforcement Learning framework designed to incentivize the generation of explicit Structural Causal Models. To prevent redundant exploration of failure states, the system utilizes a persistent artifact memory to catalog validated structural logic, functioning analogously to high-quality developer cheatsheets. Furthermore, the architecture establishes a mathematically rigorous Human-in-the-Loop protocol for undecidable edge cases and ensures continuous evaluation of long-term training dynamics. full_html:
LLMs with million-token contexts collapse out-of-distribution. The human brain, limited to 4–7 active memory slots, adapts universally. Why? Biological constraints force continuous chaos into discrete causal symbols. To achieve safe Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), we must engineer a verification substrate that mimics hominid evolution: physical invariance, adversarial tribal debate, externalized memory, and long-horizon survival.

1. Introduction: The Paradox of Unconstrained Intelligence

In the current paradigm of artificial intelligence, scaling laws dictate that greater capability requires wider contexts, billions of parameters, and the capacity to process hundreds of thousands of tokens simultaneously. Yet, a glaring paradox sits at the heart of cognitive science and machine learning:

  • The Artificial Scale Paradox: Modern Large Language Models (LLMs) possess unprecedented scale, yet they consistently fail at Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization. When the statistical correlations present in training data are inverted, or when physical rules are slightly perturbed, performance collapses into nonsensical hallucinations.

  • The Biological Bottleneck: Conversely, the biological human brain operates under a severe structural constraint—a working memory bottleneck capable of holding only 4 to 7 active concepts at any given moment. Yet, biological cognition exhibits universal adaptation: the ability to enter an entirely novel, unpredictable physical environment, extract the underlying causal invariants, and survive.

Executive Summary

The ambition to architect a stable, non-degenerative loop for Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) in artificial intelligence has historically been constrained by the verification bottleneck. As language models autonomously generate increasingly complex reasoning trajectories, codebases, and architectural modifications, the absence of an invariant, external verification mechanism invariably triggers a phenomenon identified in the proposal as Recursive Epistemic Collapse (REC). The research proposal, “Preventing Recursive Epistemic Collapse in Self-Improving AI Systems through Grounded Causal & Evolutionary Verification,” introduces a highly sophisticated, multi-layered architecture designed to mitigate this existential failure mode. By proposing a Tri-Modal Verification Sandbox, a Causal-Simplicity Reinforcement Learning (RL) reward structure based on Minimum Description Length (MDL), a compounding artifact memory, and adaptive human-in-the-loop governance, the framework seeks to ground continuous self-modification in mathematical, physical, and evolutionary realities.

This comprehensive evaluation assesses the theoretical feasibility, mathematical rigor, and practical viability of the proposed framework, cross-referencing its hypotheses with the latest advancements in algorithmic information dynamics, neurosymbolic verification, and multi-agent systems as of August 2026. The analysis concludes that the proposal is not only theoretically sound but represents a necessary paradigm shift. The integration of formal verification via Lean 4, empirical testing in physics simulators, and the penalization of algorithmic complexity via the Coding Theorem Method (CTM) directly addresses the fundamental mathematical limits of purely distributional, self-referential learning. title: Building AI that thinks before speaking
The ACWT Architecture
Beyond Bigger Datasets
desc: We’ve hit the data wall. For years, the recipe for a better language model was simple: more parameters, more tokens, more compute — scale everything together and the loss goes down. That recipe is breaking. High-quality human-written text is finite, and pouring more n...
full_html:
We’ve hit the data wall. For years, the recipe for a better language model was simple: more parameters, more tokens, more compute — scale everything together and the loss goes down. That recipe is breaking. High-quality human-written text is finite, and pouring more noisy web data into ever-larger models now buys almost nothing in exchange for enormous cost.

So the frontier has moved. Instead of asking “how do we make training bigger,” the field is now asking “how do we make thinking bigger” — spending more compute at the moment a model answers a question, not just at the moment it’s trained. This piece walks through the theory, the math, and the case studies (DeepSeek-R1 chief among them) behind that shift.

IIT-Inspired Attention

A Conceptual Architecture Proposal

Combining Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, and System-2 refinement as inductive biases for transformer attention

Scope note: This document is a design proposal, not a research report. It contains no experimental results, benchmark scores, or performance claims. The equations describe a proposed formulation to be implemented and tested; the two figures are schematic illustrations of the intended architecture and mechanism, not outputs from a trained model. An earlier draft of this material presented invented benchmark numbers as if they were measured results — those have been removed. Anything reported as fact below is either (a) established terminology from the consciousness-science literature (IIT, GWT), correctly attributed as background, or (b) a design choice being proposed for future testing.

1. Purpose and Scope

This document proposes an attention-mechanism variant, tentatively called IIT-A, that borrows structural ideas from three areas of cognitive science and complexity theory — Integrated Information Theory (IIT), Global Workspace Theory (GWT), and “System-2” deliberative reasoning — and translates them into differentiable components that could, in principle, be added to a transformer’s attention layer.

The goal is narrower than it sounds: not to build a conscious model, and not to claim any performance advantage yet, but to lay out a coherent, testable design for reducing three known failure modes of dense softmax attention:

full_html:
Scope note (read first): This document reports what is actually recorded in the project’s own artifacts: a reports-folder structure, a benchmark data-provenance log for the “IIT-A NeurIPS 2026” track, and two result summaries (a 10-seed BERT “all-plus-open” suite and a BERT-vs-RoBERTa quick comparison). It does not draw on external published literature, and it does not claim that any measured quantity (”phi,” “IB,” accuracy deltas, etc.) constitutes evidence of machine consciousness. Names such as Integrated Information Theory–Attention Modulation (IIT-AM), Consciousness Workspace Transformer (CWT), and Global Workspace are used in this report exactly as they appear in the project’s own file and method names — as engineering labels inherited from cognitive-science theories (Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory) that motivated the architecture, not as validated claims about the systems’ phenomenology. Anywhere the underlying report or provenance log does not specify a number, method, or citation, this document says so explicitly rather than inventing one.

Abstract

This report consolidates the current state of a multi-track research program that benchmarks attention-mechanism variants — inspired by, and named after, cognitive-science constructs (Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory) — against standard NLP and reasoning benchmarks. The program is organized into roughly a dozen parallel “report tracks” (Global Workspace, Selective Broadcast, Functional Consciousness, Conscious Attention, CWT/CWT Full/CWT v2, ACWT, IIT-AM v1/v2, IIT4, IIT-A, IIT Attention Variants, IIT-BERT v3 Dual-Stream, and Saliency), each with its own manuscript source, compiled PDF, and machine-readable result contracts (CSV/JSON/TXT).
